meta.scope: Afghanistan Batch 4 — Education restrictions (girls), health outcomes, and merchandise trade densification under highly constrained conditions.

candidates.title: Education enrolment and girls’ secondary exclusion statistics
candidates.publisher: Derived from UNICEF and education monitoring sources
candidates.description: Statistics and framing of education access. Afghanistan remains the only country where secondary and higher education are effectively closed to girls and women; more than 2.6 million girls have been denied secondary education since 2021. The ban is a major human-capital and long-term growth constraint.
candidates.notes: Highest-centrality education node under current restrictions. Directly linked to the women’s exclusion node.

candidates.title: Life expectancy and health outcome statistics
candidates.description: Life expectancy at birth and related health indicators. Life expectancy remains among the lowest in the region; gains earlier in the century have been partially reversed. Continuously referenced in humanitarian and human-development analysis.
candidates.notes: Core health-outcome densification under constrained service delivery.

candidates.title: Merchandise trade statistics
candidates.publisher: Derived from World Bank and trade monitoring sources
candidates.description: Statistics on merchandise exports and imports. Exports are small and concentrated in food products and textiles; India, Iran, Uzbekistan and China are notable destinations. Imports of essential goods dominate; the trade deficit is structural.
candidates.notes: Core formal trade densification under constrained conditions.

candidates.title: Afghanistan education–health–trade densification meta-node
candidates.publisher: Derived from education, health and trade sources
candidates.description: Meta-node binding education enrolment and girls’ secondary exclusion, life expectancy/health outcomes, and merchandise trade statistics into a coherent human-capital and external layer under highly constrained conditions.
